summary.text: Marcus Molinaro is the Republican candidate for the New York State Assembly, District 102, in the November 3, 2026 general election, in which he faces Democrat Janet Tweed.
He is a former Dutchess County executive and U.S. representative who served as administrator of the Federal Transit Administration from August 2025 to February 2026.

paragraphs.text: Marcus Molinaro lives in Red Hook, New York, and earned an A.S. in humanities and social sciences from Dutchess Community College in 1995.
Ballotpedia lists his career experience as including work as a real estate salesperson, county executive of Dutchess County and second vice president of the New York State Association of Counties.
Molinaro served in the New York State Assembly, District 103, from 2007 to 2012, and Didi Barrett succeeded him.
He was the Republican nominee for governor of New York in 2018 and lost to incumbent Andrew Cuomo, receiving 36.2% of the vote.
He represented New York's 19th Congressional District in the U.S. House from 2023 to 2025, after which Josh Riley succeeded him.
He served as Administrator of the U.S. Federal Transit Administration from August 2, 2025, to February 20, 2026.
The Republican primary for Assembly District 102 on June 23, 2026 was canceled, and Molinaro advanced to the general election.
